facts.text: Sandwich was founded in 1855 when Almon Gage donated land for a depot on the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy Railroad.
The town was briefly called Newark Station before being renamed Sandwich in 1856 by John Wentworth, who named it after his hometown in New Hampshire.
The historic 1879 City Hall and Opera House in Sandwich, listed on the National Register in 1979, was restored in 1986 and still hosts events.
Sandwich’s annual Fair, originally a livestock show, was canceled only once in 2020 due to COVID‑19, marking the first interruption in its history.
Plano Molding Company, a long‑standing manufacturer in Sandwich, produces molded plastic furniture and tackle boxes, reflecting the city’s enduring manufacturing heritage.
